summary.headline: GSP Crop Science Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% to INR558 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR73.6 crore (13.2% margin) on raw material cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 19.5% year on year to INR558 crore, driven mainly by realisations linked to higher raw material prices. EBITDA fell to INR73.6 crore from INR93.2 crore, with margin at 13.2%, and PAT dropped to INR44.6 crore from INR58.5 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose about 12% to INR944 crore, while H1 EBITDA fell to INR116 crore from INR135 crore and PAT was about INR71 crore. Management said EBITDA improved sequentially on cost optimisation and expects margins to improve in Q4 ahead of the Rabi pre-placement period, with Q3 likely subdued.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: Management said the growth came mainly from domestic B2B, with B2C also growing. Growth was majorly realisation-led, with some volume gains in certain products.

segments.name: International / exports
segments.commentary: Exports are about 20% of total business. Latin America and Southeast Asia are the growth markets. Management said growth so far has been predominantly domestic rather than export.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to stay under pressure in Q3 FY27, then recover in Q4 FY27 with better realisations and the pre-placement season.
EBITDA margins expected to keep improving sequentially in coming quarters, supported by Rabi products and Q4 pre-placement demand.
Q4 PAT margin expected to be better than Q3 (management confirmed on follow-up).
Normalised other income estimated at about INR20 million per period; H1 was boosted by a land parcel sale and FX gains.
Exports expected to rise to about 25% of revenue within 3 years; Brazil expected to be a sizable business in 2 to 3 years once registrations are in place.
capex_capacity: Backward integration plant already set up; R&D working on technicals and active ingredients to reduce import dependence.
R&D spend about 2.5% of revenue; management plans to increase it, with the rise expected from next year.
Brazil subsidiary set up about 3 years ago; small administration office opened for B2B business; platform to scale Brazil and Latin America expected in 1 to 2 years.
Patented products registrations in international markets have been in progress for about 3 years, with IPR-protected registrations expected in 2 to 3 years.
demand_pricing: Demand was subdued in domestic B2B and B2C from August to September because of dry weather and El Nino; distributors focused on liquidating stock at farmer level.
Monsoon rainfall was about 87% of the long period average, the lowest since 2015, per IMD as cited by management.
Rabi sowing delayed in some regions; southern reservoirs low; second paddy seen at risk, while chillies, grapes and pulses seen less affected.
Raw material costs rose and gross margin fell from about 40% to 34%; about 40-45% of raw material is imported, mainly from China.
Management attributed about 50% of margin pressure to raw material costs, 20-30% to supply chain issues, and about 20% to lower high-margin product sales.
Brazil: challenges from delayed customer buying, liquidity constraints, Chinese competition, and vessel availability and freight time.

qa_highlights.question: How wide is the Rabi portfolio, and how is market share positioned given the pollution and weather stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Presence is in Rabi crops such as fruits, vegetables and some pulses; a recently launched patented insecticide is helping Rabi sales. Rabi is a small share of the business, but management expects at least better growth than last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the revenue growth, and was it volume or realisation led?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly from domestic B2B, and was majorly realisation-led with some volume gains in certain products. Higher realisations came partly from raw material price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the EBITDA contraction in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher raw material costs, along with power and fuel costs and an annual manpower cost increase. Management attributed about 50% of margin pressure to raw materials, 20-30% to supply chain issues, and about 20% to lower high-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: When will margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects one more quarter of pressure, with margins returning to normal levels by Q4 FY27 as the season forecast improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised other income, excluding asset sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically about INR20 million per period; H1 was boosted by the sale of a land parcel and FX gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export contribution and medium-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 20% of total business and could reach about 25% in 3 years, with Latin America and Southeast Asia as the key growth markets.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation and China import dependence (40-45% of raw materials) continue to squeeze gross margin.
El Nino and below-normal rainfall through Oct-Dec 2026 could hit Rabi acreage, irrigation and agrochemical demand, with the south most exposed.
Brazil execution risk: registrations, logistics and vessel availability, liquidity, and competition from Chinese suppliers.
Track whether Q3 margins stay subdued and Q4 margin recovery happens as guided.
Track R&D spend rising from 2.5% of revenue and the progress of backward integration.
Other income was boosted by one-off land sale and FX gains, so H1 PAT includes non-recurring support.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and weather, but confident on the Q4 recovery and the longer-term Brazil and patented-product plans. Management was candid about cost pressures and the sluggish demand, but gave limited quantified guidance beyond Q4.
key_quotes: The first half of FY27 has been very challenging for the agrochemical industry with uneven rainfall and cost pressure across the industry affecting market conditions.
We can say almost 50% of the margin pressure was because of the raw material cost.
But I think in the Q4, we could see that the margins again coming up back to the normal levels.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects Q3 subdued and margin recovery to normal levels by Q4 FY27 on better realisations and pre-placement season, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts are quantified, and Q2 revenue growth was realisation-led with channel destocking and weak monsoon demand.

oneOffs.what: H1 FY27 other income was boosted by a one-off land sale and FX gains, which flatter H1 profit rather than Q2 revenue growth; the brief does not quantify the Q2 portion

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew about 19.5% to INR558 crore, mainly from realisations linked to higher raw material prices with only some volume gains, while EBITDA fell about 21% as gross margin dropped from about 40% to 34%; the brief does not quantify the volume contribution, and H1 land-sale and FX gains flatter profit rather than revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided margins back to normal levels by Q4 FY27 on better realisations and pre-placement season, after Q3 stays subdued; Q2 EBITDA margin was 13.2% against about 17% a year earlier (93.2 on about 486 revenue implied), with gross margin down from 40% to 34%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was discussed; the backward integration plant is already set up and capex was not discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 19.5% to INR558 crore but was majorly realisation-led with only some volume gains, and monsoon at about 87% of LPA with destocking weighs on demand, so volume growth depends on a Rabi and pre-placement recovery.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief gives no utilisation figure and no board plan for new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave limited quantified guidance and flagged Q3 as subdued with margin pressure from raw materials, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 FY27 is guided subdued, raw material costs (40-45% imported from China) keep squeezing gross margin, and El Nino and weak Rabi sowing could hit demand, though no numeric guidance was cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A recently launched patented insecticide is helping Rabi sales and R&D is working on technicals and actives, but no specific new launch date or count was given.

rows.label: Brazil and Latin America scale-up
rows.why: Brazil platform to scale in 1 to 2 years and IPR-protected registrations in 2 to 3 years, but management cited delayed buying, liquidity, Chinese competition and freight issues.

rows.label: Export share to 25% of revenue
rows.why: Exports are about 20% of business and could reach 25% in 3 years, though growth so far has been predominantly domestic.

rows.label: Sequential EBITDA recovery from cost optimisation
rows.why: Management said EBITDA improved sequentially on cost optimisation and expects margins to keep improving, with Q4 PAT margin above Q3 (confirmed on follow-up).

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q4 margin recovery, Brazil and patented-product plans but candid that raw material costs, weak monsoon and destocking pressured Q2; analysts probed the gross margin fall from 40% to 34% and the H1 PAT boost from one-offs.
